as_told.title: NASA transient lunar phenomena archive centred on Aristarchus

plain: Strange short-lived events have been seen on the Moon for centuries, from gas venting out of the surface to unexplained lights. These are known as lunar transient phenomena. The researcher Randall Carlson describes them in a 2025 episode. He says there are "hundreds of examples of the moon outgassing carbon dioxide, outgassing water vapor, things like that." If true, it would mean the Moon is less dead and unchanging than people usually picture it. An unnamed researcher in a 2026 episode tells it from another angle. That guest says NASA, the US space agency, keeps "this archive of transient lunar phenomena dating back hundreds of years", gathered from amateur and professional astronomers on Earth. In that guest's version many of the reports cluster around Aristarchus, a bright crater on the Moon. Neither teller says he saw these events himself.
